Its existence, not merely its shape, is the signal: bulk payment import is a first-class requirement for ASG Edge+ to design for from the start, not an afterthought bolted onto single-payment entry.

children.name: CON-R-124
children.detail: Bulk payments are imported: PaymentTransactionFullImport mirrors PaymentTransaction's 118 fields with no backing table of its own.

children.name: Escalations
children.detail: A single object — ExpenseEscalation — with two mutually exclusive drivers (fixed or index-based) and a four-level collar stacked on top. Escalation is not a schedule generator in its own right; it is an input the ExpenseSchedule generator consumes, and the escalated step is materialised directly onto the schedule row rather than kept in a separate history.

children.name: Fixed escalation
children.detail: The driver is a stated FixedAmount plus a free-text EscalationMethod that presumably chooses between adding a flat amount, adding a percentage, setting a new amount, or compounding — 'presumably' because EscalationMethod is typed Text rather than a code list, so its actual value space is unconstrained at the schema level. The result is materialised explicitly onto the schedule row as a three-value window (previous/current/next amount), which is the cleanest single idea in the whole engine and worth copying directly: an escalating schedule is a doubly-linked list of period rows, each of which knows its own amount and both neighbours'.

children.name: CON-R-041
children.detail: The driver is fixed: new amount = f(base or current amount, FixedAmount, EscalationMethod) — but EscalationMethod is free text, so its value space is unknown.

children.name: EscalationMethod
children.detail: The discriminator between add-flat, add-percentage, set-new-amount and compound — but stored as an unconstrained string rather than a code list.

children.name: Text (unconstrained)
children.detail: No code table backs this field; the UI may constrain it but the schema does not.

children.name: Free-text behavioural discriminator — a hazard and an open question
children.detail: A field that selects which formula runs should not be a string with an unknown value space. ASG Edge+ should type this as an enum once the actual values in use are read from the tenant.

children.name: Index-based escalation (CPI)
children.detail: EscalationIndex is a contract-agnostic, tenant-wide reference series — one row per published reading of an index like CPI, loaded in bulk by IMPORT_CPI_DATA and referenced by every escalation clause that needs it. Its own IndexAmount field is typed Percentage, which is unusual for what published indices normally are (a level, like 312.332, not a rate) and is the single fact that decides the whole CPI formula.

children.name: EscalationIndex.IndexAmount
children.detail: The published reading itself, for one month/year of one index series.

children.name: Percentage — unexpected for what CPI normally is
children.detail: CPI is normally published as an index level. Storing it as a Percentage type supports either of two readings: the field cosmetically holds a level despite its type name, or Lucernex genuinely stores the year-over-year change rate instead of the level.

children.name: Level or rate? Ranked #1 open question in escalations
children.detail: If IndexAmount is a level, the escalation formula is (IndexAmount / IndexBaseFactor) − 1; if it is already a rate, IndexBaseFactor is a dampening multiplier and the formula multiplies instead. This single fact must be confirmed — by loading two consecutive months of a known index and checking whether the values look like ~312/~313 (a level) or ~0.03 (a rate) — before any CPI code is written.

children.name: CON-R-042
children.detail: The driver is index-based: rawChange = (IndexAmount / IndexBaseFactor) − 1 — assumes IndexAmount is a level, which is unconfirmed.

children.name: CON-R-043
children.detail: An index change is applied: applied = rawChange × ExpenseSetup.CPIMultiplier.

children.name: CPI fields split across three objects
children.detail: A single CPI clause is configured across ExpenseSetup (CodeCPIIndexID, CPIMultiplier, IsCPICompounding), ExpenseEscalation (EscalationIndexID, IndexBaseFactor) and ExpenseSchedule/VirtualExpenseForecastPeriod (an IsCPI flag carried down onto each generated row). CodeCPIIndexID and EscalationIndexID may be two different ways of naming the same index series, or may serve genuinely different purposes — unresolved.

children.name: The four-level collar
children.detail: Escalation is bounded independently at four levels that all coexist on the same clause: a per-step percentage min/max, a lifetime percentage min/max across the whole clause, an absolute currency or percentage ceiling, and an expense stop above which the cost transfers to the tenant rather than continuing to escalate. A separate, asymmetric pair of increase/decrease caps exists in parallel on ExpenseSetup itself, and their precedence against this collar is unspecified.

children.name: CON-R-044
children.detail: A per-step collar exists: collared = clamp(applied, PeriodMinPercentage, PeriodMaxPercentage).

children.name: CON-R-045
children.detail: ExpenseSetup.IsCPICompounding is set: true escalates from the current amount; false escalates from BaseAmount.

children.name: CON-R-046
children.detail: A lifetime collar exists: cumulative change across all steps is clamped by LifetimeMinPercentage/LifetimeMaxPercentage.

children.name: CON-R-047
children.detail: An absolute ceiling exists: CapAmount/CapPercentage cap the escalated amount absolutely; order versus the collar above is unknown.

children.name: CON-R-048
children.detail: An expense stop exists: cost above StopAmount transfers to the tenant rather than continuing to escalate.

children.name: CON-R-049
children.detail: Increase/decrease asymmetry: ExpenseSetup.AmountIncreaseCap/AmountDecreaseCap/PercentIncreaseCap/PercentDecreaseCap are a separate, parallel collar to ExpenseEscalation's own min/max, with unspecified precedence between the two.

children.name: CON-R-040
children.detail: An escalation step falls due: a step occurs every EscalationPeriod × CodeFrequencyID units inside the clause's BeginDate..EndDate window.

children.name: Two unrelated escalation engines share no vocabulary
children.detail: ExpenseEscalation escalates a fixed expense amount. ExpenseRecovery has its own, completely separate escalation fields (EscalationPercentage, CodeEscalationPaymentMethodID, CapAmountChangePercent) that escalate a recovery cap and its escrow payment instead. They share no fields and no FK. ASG Edge+ needs both mechanisms and should name them distinctly — AmountEscalation and CapEscalation — rather than trying to unify two genuinely different concepts.

children.name: Rebuild typing & integrity hazards (Constitution §4.4)
children.detail: Seven rules stated as requirements on ASG Edge+ rather than observations about Lucernex — derived directly from the hazards found while reading every other branch of this map. The headline fact: every one of the 1,194 leaf fields cross-mapped into the landed Postgres schema across 33 tables is TEXT except 31 primary keys — there is no numeric, date or boolean column anywhere in the landed data, including money.

children.name: CON-R-131
children.detail: Migrating any landed Postgres column: every column across 33 tables is TEXT except 31 VARCHAR(64) primary keys — no numeric, date or boolean column exists; every value must be parsed and validated on ingest.

children.name: CON-R-132
children.detail: Migrating PaymentTransaction: AmountInvoiced and AmountReceived are declared Text while their siblings are Currency; parse to BigDecimal and reconcile.

children.name: CON-R-133
children.detail: Migrating LandlordInvoiceItem: money, date and boolean all stored as text on the reconciliation grid; replace the seven PayTrans* mirror fields with a join.

children.name: CON-R-134
children.detail: Migrating any parent-child edge: seven FKs are declared Text rather than typed, though the target's proper FK type exists elsewhere in the same schema; model them as real FKs with an orphan-handling policy.

children.name: CON-R-135
children.detail: Any usage-based rent arithmetic: 6-decimal precision is required on unit rates; use BigDecimal with explicit scale and rounding mode, never a binary float.

children.name: CON-R-136
children.detail: Any percentage arithmetic: sTYPE_PERCENTAGE fields multiply money in the pro-rata, breakpoint and CPI paths; store as BigDecimal and fix the scale and rounding policy at every multiplication step.

children.name: CON-R-137
children.detail: Any recovery measure is unset: a zero default produces spurious 100% variances; model recovery measures as nullable BigDecimal instead.

children.name: This is not precedent for §4.4's JSON-numerics-as-strings clause
children.detail: The Constitution allows JSON numeric attributes to be stored as strings and parsed under a defined schema and validation discipline. Lucernex's landed schema looks superficially similar — everything is TEXT — but without any of that discipline: no schema, no validation, no distinction between a value that will deliberately be parsed as a decimal and one that is simply untyped. ASG Edge+ should read this hazard as the failure mode §4.4 exists to prevent, not as a precedent to follow.
